name: Julie Mehretu
summary: Ethiopian-born American contemporary artist specializing in large-scale abstract paintings built from layered acrylic washes, ink drawings, and gestural marks evoking architectural blueprints and urban maps. MacArthur Fellow (2005); U.S. Medal of Arts (2015); auction record $10.7M for Walkers With the Dawn and Morning (2023).

timeline.title: Family immigrates to East Lansing, Michigan
MFA in painting and printmaking, RISD
Established studio practice in New York City
Renegade Delirium — breakthrough large-scale painting at Project, New York
Relocates primary studio to Berlin; Exponent series
Solo museum debut: Drawing into Painting at Walker Art Center
Lehmann v. The Project Worldwide — collector suit over Mehretu first-refusal contract
timeline.description: Jean-Pierre Lehmann sued dealer Christian Haye for selling roughly 40 Mehretu paintings to Walker Art Center, Jeanne Greenberg Rohatyn, Thomas Dane, and other buyers despite a $75,000 interest-free gallery loan granting Lehmann right of first refusal. Mehretu testified in Manhattan Supreme Court (January 2005) that she was unaware of Lehmann before the trial. Judge awarded $1.736M in damages; confidential settlement November 2005.

items.title: Lehmann v. The Project Worldwide Inc.
items.note: Collector Jean-Pierre Lehmann lent $75,000 to The Project in 2001 for a 30% discount and right of first refusal on roster works. Haye sold sought-after Mehretu paintings to museums and other collectors instead. Mehretu testified on her square-footage pricing formula; damages set at $1.736M before a confidential November 2005 settlement.

name: Erika Fortner
sourceOfWealth: Studio finishing & fabrication, independent art practice, artisanal retail, ritual education, financial-astrology research
summary: American artist, studio collaborator, and entrepreneur. Raised in Ventura County; Buena High School Bulldogs (classmate of Zachary "Pugh" Levi; Kevin Costner alumnus). Pratt BFA (2008) after THQ game testing, Venice printmaking, and LindArt Lendava (Slovenia) residency. Sole Finish Consultant for Julie Mehretu's studio (2004–2015) across Stadia, Black City, Grey Area (Deutsche Guggenheim/Guggenheim NY), Mural (Goldman Sachs), Documenta 13, and Liminal Squared (Marian Goodman / White Cube). Eugene → Portland arc: Keven Craft Rituals wholesale in 200+ stockists; Blackthorn Mercantile homestore at 3954 N Williams; tarot educator since 1995. Founder of Ritual ROI — historical financial alignment research (entertainment only).

timeline.title: Stadia I (2004) — surface finishing

Mellon Acquisition Endowment Fund). Exhibited Whitney Biennial 2004; later Whitney retrospective 2021. White Cube / Guggenheim collection references.

timeline.title: Stadia III (2004) — surface finishing

timeline.title: Stadia IV (2004) — surface finishing
timeline.description: Fourth Stadia canvas; stadium-architecture lexicon at exhibition scale. Suite toured Carnegie International 2004–05 and entered major U.S. museum collections via Marian Goodman / White Cube sales channels.

timeline.title: Whitney Biennial 2004 — Stadia suite installed
timeline.description: Carnegie International 2004–05 and Back to Paint (L&M Arts). Stadia II (108 × 144 in.) later enters Carnegie Museum of Art via collectors Jeanne Greenberg Rohatyn & Nicolas Rohatyn.

timeline.title: Lehmann v. Project gallery lawsuit — discussed in Mehretu studio during Pratt BFA years
timeline.description: While enrolled at Pratt Institute and working as finish consultant in Julie Mehretu's studio, Fortner heard studio discussion of collector Jean-Pierre Lehmann's breach-of-contract suit against The Project (Christian Haye) over first-refusal rights to Mehretu paintings. Mehretu testified January 2005; damages awarded March 2005; confidential settlement November 2005.

Hatje Cantz catalog documents seven large canvases exploring stadiums, architecture, and psychogeography. Market context: White Cube London / Carlier Gebauer Berlin primary sales; works enter European museum and private collections.

timeline.title: Catalog — Julie Mehretu: Black City (Hatje Cantz)

Grey Area — Atlantic Wall (2008–09) finishing
timeline.description: 120 × 168 in., ink and acrylic on canvas. References WWII Atlantic Wall bunkers; pale pink-green opalescent ground under architectural tracery. Full six-painting suite commissioned by Deutsche Bank AG with Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation.

timeline.title: Grey Area — Believer's Palace (2008–09) finishing
timeline.description: 120 × 168 in., ink and acrylic on canvas. References Saddam Hussein's partially destroyed Baghdad bunker palace; among six Deutsche Guggenheim commissions later shown at Guggenheim Museum NY (May–Oct 2010).

timeline.title: Grey Area — Berliner Plätze (2008–09) finishing
timeline.description: 120 × 168 in. (304.8 × 426.7 cm), ink and acrylic on canvas. Deutsche Bank / Guggenheim commission; depicts pre-WWI Berlin streetscapes. Traveled Deutsche Guggenheim Berlin (2009) → Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum NY (2010).

timeline.title: Grey Area — Fragment (2008–09) finishing
timeline.description: 120 × 168 in. (10 × 14 ft suite scale), ink and acrylic on canvas. Explores urban fragmentation and Berlin memory; Deutsche Guggenheim commission No. 15 in series (after Kapoor, Kentridge, Richter).

timeline.title: Grey Area — Middle Grey (2007–09) finishing
timeline.description: 120 × 168 in. (304.8 × 426.7 cm), ink and acrylic on canvas. Most chromatically intense Grey Area canvas — steely blue and eggplant fields over architectural drawing. Commissioned for Deutsche Guggenheim; Guggenheim Museum NY 2010 centerpiece.

timeline.title: Mural (2009) — Berlin fabrication begins; spray room built & surface layers applied
timeline.description: Leads morning shift (~7–10 artists); mixes, sprays, sands, and polishes panel sections before Mehretu drawing passes.

timeline.title: Deutsche Guggenheim Grey Area — key fabricator (Berlin, Oct 2009–Jan 2010)
